Read the approach

Built a natural-language analytics space from scratch on Databricks Genie. Standardised 134 metrics across roughly 40 tables and 20 metric views. Added business terminology and sample SQL to turn plain-English questions into reliable answers.

Benchmarked on about 100 questions with ground-truth SQL, sourced from BU analysts (commonly used metrics plus problem areas from previous and current cycles). Refined metric definitions and example queries against recurring failure patterns: confusion between similar-named metrics, wrong grain, and NTILE-based bucketing where order-contribution (OC) percentage buckets were needed.

Trust safeguards: escalation rule to validate high-stakes numbers with an analyst, plus a feedback loop for wrong answers. Adoption driven by training, weekly rewards and champions, and a pod-by-pod rollout.

July 2025 · Product case study · With Utkarsh Rathor

Operational optimisation & user retention for Rapido

Making bike-taxi, auto and cab rides more reliable, safer and worth returning to.

1 / 16Swipe through the deckOpen full deck ↗
Read the approach and impact

Approach

Surveyed 250+ users. Built two personas: Rajat, 28, sales executive in Gurgaon (reliable bookings, instant rematching), and Aditi, 23, MBA student in Mumbai (verified captains, a stable app in weak-network areas). Mapped the bike-taxi booking journey and its pain points. RICE prioritisation surfaced four areas: captain reliability, rider safety, technical accessibility and loyalty.

Designed three solutions:

  • Safe Captains Only: safety badges for captains with verified helmets and strong ride histories, plus a filter matching riders only with top-rated, safety-verified captains.
  • Rapido Lite: lightweight, offline-resilient app for Tier-2/3 cities and weak-network zones, with an auto-prompt to switch on low signal.
  • Automatic rematching with captain penalty points: instant reassignment to the next-best captain after a cancellation, with penalties for unjustified cancellations and safety violations.

Projected impact

Projected, not measured. Survey-based model over a one-month window:

  • Safe Captains Only: about 6,100 users with safety concerns, 30% adoption (about 1,830 users), average ride rating up 0.13 to 4.43.
  • Rapido Lite: about 2,800 users facing app crashes, 70% adoption, booking failure rate cut from 20% to 10%, about 980 bookings recovered per month.
  • Rematching and penalty points: about 5,100 users facing cancellations, lost rides down from about 2,040 to 653 per month, about 1,387 rides saved per month.
March 2025 · Business case study

Fresh Bites profitability case study

Finding the profit leak behind growing revenue.

1 / 7Swipe through the deckOpen full deck ↗
Read the approach and impact

Approach

Revenue grew from ₹230 million to ₹270 million while profit margin fell from 26.1% to 23.3%. Decline traced to the online channel: profitability down from 23.1% to 18.8%, labour cost up 53.8% against 23% online revenue growth, and delivery cost at 25% of online revenue against 18–20% at competitors. Product-level cost analysis and benchmarking pointed to salads (65% cost of goods sold, against 58–60% at competitors) as the least efficient category.

Projected impact

Projected, not measured: ₹8.7 million combined profit impact from three levers: salad cost of goods sold cut from 65% to 60% (about ₹3 million), a wraps marketing push at 50% ROI (₹1 million net gain), and online delivery savings through logistics partnerships and automation.
